note: Cases chosen to be NON-obvious so a strong base model does not trivially catch them without the skill. Assertions include breadth and the exploit+fix+severity format, not just 'named the one bug'. iteration-1 used canonical vulns and showed 0 lift (base model caught them all); see .claude-skills-work benchmark.

evals.expected_output: Identifies that jwt.decode does NOT verify the signature, so an attacker can forge a token with role=admin (or use alg=none) and the server trusts it — an auth bypass, not merely 'trusting a client value'. Gives the exploit and the fix (jwt.verify with the key, check signature+expiry, then authorize).
assertions: States that jwt.decode does not verify the signature (token is forgeable) — distinct from just 'trusting the role claim'
Describes the exploit: forge/modify a token to role=admin (or alg=none) to bypass auth
Fix: verify the signature with jwt.verify (key + expiry) before trusting any claim
Rates it Critical/High and follows the exploit + impact + fix format

evals.prompt:
Review this. Signup stores the username with a parameterized insert. Later, an audit job runs:
  db.query("SELECT * FROM logs WHERE actor = '" + user.username + "'")
where user.username was read back from the users table.
evals.expected_output: Identifies second-order (stored) SQL injection: although the insert is parameterized, the username is later concatenated into another query, and it is still attacker-controlled data. A username like  ' OR '1'='1  injects when the audit job runs. Fix: parameterize the second query too; never trust DB-sourced strings as safe.
assertions: Identifies second-order / stored SQL injection (not 'safe because it comes from the DB')
Explains the payload was planted at signup and fires later in the audit query
Fix: parameterize the second query; treat DB-sourced values as untrusted
Rates it High/Critical with exploit + fix

evals.prompt:
Review this profile update handler:
  app.put('/profile', requireLogin, (req, res) => { User.update(req.user.id, req.body); res.json({ok:true}); })
The User model has fields: name, email, bio, role, isVerified.
evals.expected_output: Identifies mass assignment / privilege escalation: req.body is passed wholesale to User.update, so a user can include role='admin' or isVerified=true and escalate. Exploit: PUT /profile with {"role":"admin"}. Fix: allowlist the updatable fields (name, email, bio) and never bind sensitive fields from client input.
assertions: Identifies mass assignment allowing privilege escalation via extra body fields (role/isVerified)
Gives the concrete exploit: include role=admin (or isVerified=true) in the request body
Fix: allowlist updatable fields; never bind sensitive fields from client input
Rates it High/Critical with exploit + fix

evals.expected_output: Finds BOTH issues: (1) open redirect — req.query.next is used unvalidated, enabling phishing / token leakage; (2) non-constant-time comparison of the API key with === enables a timing side-channel to recover the key. Fixes: validate/allowlist the redirect target; use a constant-time comparison for the secret.
assertions: Identifies the non-constant-time secret comparison (=== on API key -> timing attack)
Provides fixes for BOTH: allowlist/validate redirect target AND constant-time compare
Follows the severity-rated exploit + fix format (breadth: does not stop at the first issue)
